topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

outline.topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

sections.title: Hook & Prerequisite Review (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly revisit the macroscopic definition of the refractive index (n = c/v). Introduce the concept of the Lorentz Oscillator Model, viewing electrons in an atom as masses on springs connected to the nucleus.
sections.example: A plucked guitar string: atoms vibrate at a 'natural frequency' when light waves interact with them.

sections.title: The Microscopic Origin (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain how an incoming electromagnetic wave induces an oscillation in the electron cloud. This oscillation generates a secondary wave. The interference between the incident wave and the secondary wave results in a phase delay, manifesting as a slower propagation velocity (n > 1).
sections.example: Visualize a crowd (electrons) reacting to a runner (light wave). The crowd's delay in parting creates a 'slowed down' effect for the runner's path.

sections.title: Color Dependence: Dispersion (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Connect the frequency of the light wave (color) to the oscillator model. When light frequency approaches the natural frequency of the atom, the oscillation amplitude increases significantly. Use a graph showing n(ω) vs. ω to demonstrate the resonance effect.
sections.example: A swing being pushed: if you push at the natural frequency (resonance), the amplitude is huge; if not, the response is weaker.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization & Conclusion (3:30-5:00)
sections.content: Present the Cauchy dispersion equation n(λ) = A + B/λ². Use an animation where a white light beam enters a prism; the screen shows how different wavelengths (colors) follow different paths due to varying refractive indices.
sections.example: A 'Rainbow Prism' simulation showing blue light (shorter wavelength, higher n) bending more sharply than red light (longer wavelength, lower n).

storyboard.title: Hook & Prerequisite Review (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Refractive index defines how light slows down.
We model electrons as masses on springs.
Atoms have a natural vibration frequency.
animations: Create text 'Light Interaction' at center, color #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Microscopic Origin (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Oscillating electrons emit a secondary wave.
The result is a refractive index above one.
animations: Visualize atoms as small spheres, color #00FF00.
Show atom vibrating in response to wave, color #FF0000.

storyboard.title: Color Dependence: Dispersion (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: Light color relates to its frequency.
Oscillation amplitude depends on light frequency.
Resonance occurs near the natural frequency.
animations: Show light splitting into spectrum colors, #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF.

storyboard.title: Mathematical Visualization & Conclusion (3:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Light enters a prism at an angle.
Colors bend based on their wavelength.
animations: Show mathematical formula for dispersion in #FFFFFF.
